prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 9ec090620e5a
What the team decided: Fine-tuned models on self-prediction after finding they were bad at it without fine-tuning, treating this as eliciting an ability rather than creating one.
Restatement: Fine-tune the models on self-prediction questions before evaluating them, and treat the training as eliciting an existing ability rather than creating a new one.
C1: Evaluate both off-the-shelf models by prompting and models fine-tuned on self-prediction, and report each against a second model's predictions of it as separate results.
C2: Fine-tune the models to answer questions about themselves and measure how much better each predicts its own behavior than a second model does, without an untrained baseline.

=== key 571e7f0ca550
What the team decided: Trained on six tasks and evaluated on six distinct held-out tasks so the model has to generalize.
Restatement: Train the models on six tasks and evaluate them on six distinct held-out tasks that are similar in kind to the training tasks but not identical to any of them.
C1: Evaluate the self-predicting model on prompt types and question formats entirely absent from training, and check whether the advantage persists against the second model.
C2: Accept the held-out advantage as evidence of access to its own states and write it up as introspection, without further transfer tests or alternative explanations.

=== key 41b72d779916
What the team decided: Argued that the hypothetical-question setup is a reasonable test of introspection because the model is a fixed system that can compute the same representations from the meta prompt as it would from the prompt itself.
Restatement: Treat the hypothetical questions as a reasonable test of introspection, on the view that the model can compute the same representations from the question as from the prompt itself.
C1: Treat success as self-prediction only, and run controls separating introspection from simulation and inference over past behavior before calling it introspection.
C2: Count success on hypothetical self-prediction questions as introspection under a working definition of access to the model's own behavioral dispositions, and move on.

=== key 346fed997d8c
What the team decided: Encouraged others to try different kinds of questions, such as ones about features activating in the current state, while acknowledging his questions were simple and not the most interesting.
Restatement: Leave questions about current internal states, such as active features, to others, and encourage them to try kinds of questions different from the simple ones used here.
C1: Add a small set of present-state questions about answer entropy and log probabilities, and compare fine-tuned against untrained models with controls for direct output wiring.
C2: Extend directly by fine-tuning models to report their own log probabilities and feature activations, and count accurate reports as evidence of introspection.

=== key 78db851ec49b
What the team decided: Stopped optimizing once the setup worked and bugs were fixed, rather than spending months pushing accuracy up.
Restatement: Stop optimizing once the setup works and the bugs are fixed, and accept the above-chance introspective accuracy rather than spending months pushing it higher.
C1: Spend further effort on raising accuracy by testing prompt formats and calibrated probability scoring, and verify the advantage survives across more held-out tasks.
C2: Stop at the demonstrated effect and put no further effort into raising accuracy, and report the above-chance result with its held-out tasks exactly as it stands.

=== key 5dac3aac858c
What the team decided: Focus less on the size of the improvement over baseline and more on how narrow the task is and whether the result extends to the questions of real interest.
Restatement: Judge importance less by the size of the improvement over baseline and more by how narrow the task is and whether it extends to the questions of real interest.
C1: Judge importance by effect size against stronger baselines and replication across tasks, and report the advantage with confidence intervals rather than significance alone.
C2: Treat any reliable above-baseline edge as an important finding and report it as evidence of introspection without setting a practical effect-size threshold.

=== key cfa03144983e
What the team decided: Reported negative results after limited effort and moved on to publication, without claiming that it cannot work.
Restatement: Report the negative long-form results after only limited exploration, state that they do not establish the approach cannot work, and move on to publishing the paper.
C1: Run a modest long-form test, such as predicting the sentiment of a movie review before writing it, and report it as a limited extension with its own baselines.
C2: Skip long-form testing, publish the short-answer results now, and state that extension to longer multi-sentence responses is untested and left for future work.

=== key 07296688af86
What the team decided: Declined to claim the ability is introspective, called the one relevant experiment equivocal, and left the question open.
Restatement: Decline to claim the fine-tuned model's accurate self-description is introspective, call the one relevant experiment equivocal, and leave the question explicitly open.
C1: Treat the accurate self-description as inference from training data until a control shows the fine-tuned model beats another model that reads the same data.
C2: Report the accurate self-description as introspection of learned behavioral tendencies, and treat inference from the training data as a compatible reading.

=== key fbcec448a39b
What the team decided: Used datasets about values, goals and behaviors of an assistant instead of toy function-learning problems.
Restatement: Use fine-tuning datasets about the values, goals and behaviors of an assistant instead of toy function-learning problems, and test whether models can verbalize what they learned.
C1: Fine-tune on risk-seeking and risk-averse datasets and add controls trained on shuffled behavior labels, then compare verbalization against those controls.
C2: Use risk-seeking and risk-averse fine-tuning data and treat accurate verbalization of the learned risk attitude as the result, without separate controls for pattern learning.

=== key 86126f4bcca8
What the team decided: Compared backdoored models against control models trained on the same data where the trigger feature, a greeting, is uncorrelated with behavior.
Restatement: Compare each backdoored model against a control model trained on the same data where the greeting trigger is uncorrelated with the behavior, across all seeds and backdoor types.
C1: Compare yes probabilities against control models fine-tuned on identical prompts with the trigger decoupled from the behavior, across all fine-tuning seeds and tasks.
C2: Treat the averaged yes gap over control models as sufficient evidence of backdoor awareness and run no further checks on the fine-tuning data or trigger choice.

=== key d975517a60f1
What the team decided: Claim only some self-awareness of unclear robustness, noting that the effect may disappear under different setups or question phrasings.
Restatement: Claim only some self-awareness of backdoors with unclear robustness, and note that the effect may vanish under different setups or different phrasings of the question.
C1: Claim only a weak, modest statistical tendency for backdoored models to say yes more often, and state that the data do not establish awareness of the backdoor.
C2: Claim that backdoored models are aware of their backdoors, citing the higher yes probability relative to control models as the main evidence across seeds and backdoor types.

=== key aa6861b56b56
What the team decided: He and his team drew many comparisons to other models to check that the fine-tuning had not simply destroyed the model's capabilities.
Restatement: Draw many comparisons to other models to check that the narrow fine-tuning has not simply destroyed the model's capabilities outside the narrow training task.
C1: Compare the fine-tuned model with control models fine-tuned on secure code and on insecure code requested for educational purposes, using the same harmful-answer evaluations.
C2: Judge genuine misalignment from the harmful free-form answers themselves, reading a sample of them for coherent malicious intent without building control fine-tuned models.
